extracted.intended_audience: neuroscientists, cognitive/affective researchers, and scholars studying humor processing
extracted.subtask_description: A synthesis and model describing the neural systems that detect/resolve incongruity and that generate affective appreciation/reward for humorous stimuli, plus factors that modulate their coupling. Useful for researchers aiming to explain or predict when and why stimuli elicit amusement or laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-network architecture (overall model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor processing is best characterized as the coupling of two distinct networks: a cognitive network for detection/resolution of incongruity and an affective network for appreciation/reward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete account must specify how the cognitive network processes the comic structure and how the affective network rewards successful comprehension. Emphasize the coupling between systems rather than treating humor as a single process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network 1: Detection & resolution of incongruity (cognitive)
rubrics_metrics.description: A cortical network that detects mismatches between expected and presented stimuli and carries out reinterpretation/resolution (temporoparietal junction, posterior temporal regions, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, inferior frontal gyrus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions include mismatch detection (temporo-occipital-parietal junction), script/script comparison (posterior temporal), working memory and conflict monitoring during reinterpretation (DLPFC), and semantic/phonological resolution (IFG). Assess whether stimulus structure engages these processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network 2: Appreciation & reward (affective)
rubrics_metrics.description: A subcortical/limbic network that generates subjective amusement and reward responses (mesocorticolimbic dopaminergic system — VTA, nucleus accumbens, vmPFC; and amygdala for salience/emotional valuation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful engagement of the cognitive network can trigger mesolimbic reward circuitry; measure or predict activity in ventral striatum, VTA, vmPFC and amygdala as indices of affective response to humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence of processing (temporal flow)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor processing proceeds from stimulus arrival → mismatch detection → cognitive resolution → reward activation → motor output (laughter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical sequence: (1) temporo-occipital-parietal detection of mismatch, (2) cortical comprehension network (DLPFC + temporal regions) attempts resolution, (3) if resolution succeeds mesolimbic reward circuit fires producing subjective amusement, (4) motor output (laughter) via brainstem and cerebellar pathways. Use this ordering when designing experiments or interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex differences in reward activation
rubrics_metrics.description: Sex modulates reward activation: women show greater reward activation per unit of 'funniness' (more selective), men show similar reward activation across a wider range of stimuli (less discriminating), while both sexes activate the same network architecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When predicting or measuring humorous response, account for sex-based differences in reward sensitivity/selectivity even if cognitive processing appears similar across sexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personality (extraversion) effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Extraverts show stronger ventral striatal response to humor; introverts show weaker reward responses; comprehension network remains unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider individual differences in extraversion as a predictor of reward-circuit engagement; extraversion modulates affective response without altering cognitive resolution capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age-related modulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Developmental and aging effects: children’s comprehension networks mature gradually (physical/incongruity humor understood earlier than complex verbal humor); older adults preserve appreciation but show slower comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calibrate stimulus complexity to audience age: use simpler, less ToM-dependent structures for younger children; expect slower processing speed in older adults even if reward circuitry remains engaged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychiatric/clinical condition effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical conditions alter coupling or components: autism alters theory-of-mind processing affecting social/sarcastic humor comprehension; depression reduces mesolimbic response leading to reduced enjoyment despite intact comprehension; schizophrenia disrupts incongruity-resolution coupling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for condition-specific disruptions (e.g., ToM deficits in autism, blunted reward in depression) when evaluating humor comprehension or designing stimuli for clinical populations; calibration may be necessary to match abilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensibility to the audience (cognitive prerequisites)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funniness depends on whether the audience can comprehend the stimulus given their script knowledge, language facility, theory-of-mind capacity, and age-appropriate complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and match jokes to audience’s vocabulary, cultural/script knowledge, and ToM competence; incomprehensible or overly complex structure will block downstream reward responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reward-engagement matched to the audience (affective state)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funniness depends on the audience’s reward system state (mood, extraversion, reward sensitivity, attention to social vs structural features) and whether the stimulus engages those valuation processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider and, if possible, prime mood/attention and tailor content to whether the audience responds more to social/emotional features or structural/semantic surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity of coupling between cognitive and affective networks
rubrics_metrics.description: A stimulus must not only be comprehensible and rewarding in isolation but must successfully couple comprehension with reward — some populations may have one without the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both networks: ensure cognitive resolution leads to reward activation. For populations with coupling disruptions, modify structure or reward cues to increase the likelihood of coupling (e.g., simpler jokes, more salient rewards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic checklist for audience calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical diagnostic questions to evaluate whether a joke will work for a given audience: (1) cognitive prerequisites (vocabulary, scripts, ToM), (2) reward state (mood, extraversion, attention), (3) calibration for known coupling disruptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these three questions to adapt material: verify comprehension capacities, assess reward/attentional readiness, and for populations with known coupling issues (children, autism, depression, schizophrenia) simplify structure or reduce ToM demands as needed.
